description: Superimposes miniature copies of each source 'wavecycle' onto itself: every wavecycle is shrunk by the integer scaling divisor and the shorter, higher copies are layered over the original. Duration model static and sample-exact (frame counts identical to the input on 1 s and 2 s tone and noise probes). Mono only.
musical_use: A powerful and somewhat wild distortion tool. Because scaling is a divisor, higher values make the superimposed copies shorter and higher - heard as a sheen of distortion floating above the original sound; low values (2-4) add gritty octave-up-like artefacts fused with the source. loudness balances input against the processed component: 1.0 keeps the original at full level with the superimpositions on top; below 1 recedes the fractal layer into a halo; above 1 lets it dominate (be careful - it can grow well past clipping). Both scaling and loudness take breakpoint files, so the sheen can sweep upward or fade in across the sound.

scaling.description: Integer division of the scale of the source wave (range 2 to sample_rate/2 - CDP-enforced, so the maximum is input-dependent: at 44.1 kHz the binary rejects 30000 with 'Value (30000.000000) out of range (2.000000 to 22050.000000)'). Higher values give shorter, higher-pitched superimposed copies - more of a 'sheen'. May vary over time (banner-confirmed; probe verified - a 2->64 breakpoint render differs from both endpoint scalar renders).

loudness.description: Loudness of the scaled component relative to the source, whose loudness is reckoned as 1.0 (CDP-enforced range 0.000031-32767; the documented working range is 0-10 and values above 1 amplify the fractal layer - use with care). May vary over time (banner-confirmed; probe verified against both endpoint renders).

pre_attenuation.description: Gain multiplier applied to the input before processing, to make headroom for the superimposed copies (CDP-enforced range 0.000031-32767 - despite the name, values above 1 are accepted and amplify). Scalar only - a breakpoint file is refused.

examples.expected_use: Original clearly audible with a gritty, higher partial layer welded on; duration unchanged.

examples.description: High sheen fading in over the sound.
examples.expected_use: A high distortion sheen that rises from nearly inaudible to source level across a 2 s file (loudness as a breakpoint envelope).

known_issues: loudness and pre_attenuation accept values far beyond the documented 0-10 / attenuation-only ranges (CDP enforces 0.000031-32767 for both); large values can push the output well past full scale.
scaling's maximum is sample_rate/2, so the enforced range varies with the input file's sample rate.
pre_attenuation rejects breakpoint files: 'ERROR: Cannot read parameter 3 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.'
Mono only: a stereo input is refused with 'Application doesn't work with this type of infile.' (exit 255).
